jobs.title: Director of Development for Athletics (Administrator II)
jobs.description:
Shape the future at SSU!

Director of Development for Athletics

It is an exciting time to join Sonoma State University as we launch the Director of Development for Athletics search! Sonoma State University is seeking a highly motivated, relationship-driven individual who will serve as a vital component of the educational experience at Sonoma State, emphasizing the importance of academic achievement alongside athletic success. In fall 2027, Sonoma State Athletics will have 10 NCAA Division II teams competing in the California Collegiate Athletic Association conference as part of the broader reimagining of the university and its programs. Seawolf Athletics represents an exciting investment in student life, campus pride, and the future of Sonoma State. This position will have the unique opportunity during this monumental time to manage and cultivate a portfolio of major gift prospects and fundraising efforts to support the Intercollegiate Athletics Program and future programming efforts. The ideal candidate in this role should have a positive attitude, an active, energetic mind, and a leadership style that is characterized by highly ethical practices and a commitment to inclusivity, openness, flexibility, integrity, and kindness.

About Us

Sonoma State’s Intercollegiate Athletics Program is committed to providing quality experience for all student-athletes, focusing on fair play, sportsmanship, and teamwork. It also aims to enhance the University’s mission by fostering pride and involvement among students, faculty, staff, alumni, and community members. We are committed to achieving excellence through teaching, scholarship, learning and inclusion. In line with our Strategic Plan and our Seawolf Commitment, the University values include diversity, sustainability, community engagement, respect, responsibility, excellence and integrity. We strive to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can learn and work in an atmosphere of civility and respect. We encourage innovation, experimentation and creativity, as well as contributions to equity and inclusion, in the pursuit of excellence for all members of our university community.

The Role

Reporting to the Associate Vice President of Development, working in concert with the Interim Director of Athletics, and the President, the Director of Development for Athletics establishes fundraising strategies and directs and conducts fundraising activities to secure philanthropic support for the Intercollegiate Athletics Program in alignment with Sonoma State University priorities. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, identifying, qualifying, cultivating and soliciting potential donors for the Athletics Program; organizing and providing effective communication with donors and potential donors; stewarding alumni and other individual prospects, sponsors and major donors; coordinating gift processing; recruiting, training and motivating volunteers for the university; and, other fundraising projects.

Qualifications

This position requires a minimum of four years of experience in successful relationship building with prospects, volunteers, and board members, along with a demonstrated aptitude to be successful in face-to-face fundraising, including 4 years of progressively responsible and applicable management and/or supervisory experience. Bachelor’s degree required. The incumbent must have a proven track record of successfully working with individual donors, soliciting and securing gifts and demonstrate experience in designing and implementing successful fundraising strategies. Experience in athletic fundraising within a university environment and a strong understanding of university culture and corporate partnerships highly preferred. Please review the position description for full scope of responsibilities and qualifications.

Application Deadline

This position is open until filled. For full consideration, please submit an application, resume and cover letter addressing the prompt below by 8am on Tuesday, August 11th.

Prompt:
Please describe your experience designing and implementing a comprehensive development plan for an organization, agency, or project. In addition, please describe how your qualifications and experience would directly translate to this role and support the future of fundraising for Athletics.

Salary And Benefits

Starting salary placement depends on qualifications and experience and is anticipated to be in the range of $8,334 - $8,667 a month. This position is a member of the Management Personnel Plan and serves at the pleasure of the President. This position is eligible for a broad range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurances, retirement (CalPERS), tuition waiver, vacation and sick leave. In addition, 15 paid holidays are offered each year. Sonoma State University is also a Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF) Employer ( comprehensive benefits summary PDF ).

Equal Opportunity & Mandated Reporting

The University is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, medical condition, disability, marital status, or protected veteran status. Mandated Reporting: This position may be considered a "mandated reporter" under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.

Employment Eligibility & Conditions

Sonoma State University, as part of the CSU system, is a State of California Employer. As such, the University requires all employees upon date of hire to reside in the State of California. As of January 1, 2022 the CSU Out-of-State Employment Policy prohibits the hiring of employees to perform CSU-related work outside the state of California. A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily before any candidate can be offered a position. jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and providing space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

The Law School’s Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) team engages alumni philanthropically and in programming and initiatives that strengthen the school and the student experience. The mission of the Development arm is to secure financial support for core operations and special initiatives that advance the law school’s mission.

Position Overview

The position involves designing, developing, delivering, and administering fundraising programs. Develops and implements strategies for cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major gifts prospects with the capacity for a major gift of $25k to $1M and above; identifies new donor prospects through researching background information on potential donors and developing materials, creating marketing plans, and organizing related programs/events; cultivates, stewards, and solicits donor prospects for gifts ranging from $25K to $1M and above; prepares and negotiates gift instruments ranging from moderate to high complexity; works with the Dean, Assistant Dean and faculty as necessary to solicit the largest gifts; manages a portfolio of principal gift prospects assigned to the Dean. Directs the research and preparation of the Dean’s briefings materials, creates talking points and meeting strategies for the Dean and briefs the Dean on these strategies. As appropriate, staffs the Dean on principal gifts visits and directs the tracking and implementation of all follow-up; manages the activities of the campaign cabinet and their meetings; collaborates with the Director of Financial Aid and the Director of Career Services to ensure proper stewardship of financial aid donors.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is: August 12, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Fundraising

Plans, organizes, and directs large-scale fundraising campaigns for Berkeley Law.
Participates in short- and long-range strategic planning. This includes annual stewardship for existing donors, long-term planning for prospect cultivation, foundation research and strategy, and campaign planning related to Berkeley Law endowment funds and long-term fundraising initiatives.
Identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards major gift prospects and donors, using established metrics (currently CADS) to track activity and report outcomes. Utilizes a return-on-investment approach in managing a donor portfolio.
Responsible for major gifts, corporate and foundation fundraising, and direct marketing efforts that generate philanthropic support for Berkeley Law. Manages a portfolio of donors with the capacity to give between $25,000 and $1,000,000 or more.
Writes complex proposals for individual, corporate, and foundation prospects.
Travels to meet with donors and represent Berkeley Law. Designs, organizes, and attends functions, meetings, and conferences as a representative of Berkeley Law. May serve on internal and external committees as a campus or Berkeley Law representative.
May participate in cross-campus, multi-unit fundraising campaigns in partnership with UDAR.
Ensures fundraising goals are achieved and raises at least $1 million annually by:
Managing a portfolio of 75–100 major gift and corporate/foundation prospects with the capacity to give $25,000–$1,000,000+.
Making 15–20 substantive donor contacts per month that advance relationships.
Conducting 80–120 donor visits annually.
Leading the planning and evaluation of fund development and annual solicitation programs, including financial feasibility studies, market research, and recommendations for program improvements.
Closing at least $1 million in new gift commitments or outright gifts.

Volunteer Engagement

May recruit, train, and support key volunteers who assist in advancement and fundraising efforts.

Program Leadership & Administration

May oversee the work of professional and support staff involved in implementing multi-component fundraising programs.
Uses key fundraising applications and databases to support fundraising strategies, goals, and objectives.

Professional Development & Other Duties

Engages in professional development and training opportunities as appropriate.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Advanced knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations.
Advanced knowledge of UC Berkeley and Berkeley Law, including relevant issues affecting the campus and higher education.
Advanced knowledge of UC Berkeley and Berkeley Law, including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements, and organizational infrastructure.
Advanced knowledge of applicable laws, regulations, and institutional policies related to gift acceptance, prospect management, and philanthropic fundraising.
Advanced written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the political acumen to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
Advanced skill in developing persuasive and compelling presentations that effectively communicate campus priorities and secure philanthropic support.
Advanced ability to achieve established goals and objectives through effective program and project planning, organization, execution, and evaluation.
Demonstrated commitment to and understanding of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB), with the ability to integrate DEIB principles into daily work and interactions.
Demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds represented within the UC Berkeley community.
Commitment to fostering an equitable, inclusive, and welcoming environment where students, faculty, staff, alumni, and donors of all backgrounds feel respected, supported, and valued.
Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to make sound decisions, identify and resolve complex issues, and develop creative solutions.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Advanced project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint, as well as UDAR fundraising systems and the ability to quickly learn new technologies.
Experience working with alumni, donors, volunteers, and other constituent groups, with the ability to cultivate and maintain positive, productive relationships.
Demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment.
Ability to travel and work evenings, approximately twice per month, as needed.
Demonstrated ability to meet or exceed fundraising goals and performance objectives.

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

Juris Doctor (JD) degree and/or experience in legal environments.
Membership in Council Advancement Secondary Education (CASE) and/or Association of Fundraising Professionals.

This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

This is a full-time (40 hours/week) Career position eligible for UC benefits.

This position is eligible for up to 20% remote work. Exact arrangements are determined in partnership with your supervisor to meet role responsibilities and department needs and are subject to change.

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter.

This is a designated position requiring fingerprinting and a background check due to the nature of the job responsibilities. Berkeley does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities. The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts a conditional offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; received notice of any allegations or are currently the subject of any administrative or disciplinary proceedings involving misconduct; have left a position after receiving notice of allegations or while under investigation in an administrative or disciplinary proceeding involving misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of misconduct with a previous employer.

Position Overview

The CEO Fundraising Sr. Specialist will play a pivotal role in advancing fundraising efforts led by the President and CEO, recognized as Women's World Banking's most effective fundraising asset. In this role, you will work in direct partnership with the CEO to identify, develop, and advance a strong pipeline and portfolio of prospective supporters, helping create opportunities that contribute to the organization's long-term fundraising goals.

A significant element of this work involves supporting the implementation of the CEO’s fundraising strategy and the development of a principal gifts pipeline under her leadership. You will be responsible for building and advancing a robust pipeline of prospective supporters, creating a disciplined cultivation process that generates a steady flow of new and engaged donors. This work supports the CEO's fundraising objectives, which include securing $10 million annually, representing approximately half of the organization's overall fundraising target, with at least half of that funding being unrestricted. While the organization's broader fundraising strategy is developed by senior leadership, the CEO defines the fundraising strategy and priorities needed to achieve her fundraising goals within that framework. This role is responsible for helping to bring that strategy to life through generating opportunities, advancing prospects, and contributing to fundraising objectives.

Success in this role requires a combination of strong research and analytical skills, sound judgment, persistence, and a sales-minded approach to relationship development. The ideal candidate is energized by opening doors, connecting the dots across networks, creating momentum, and helping move relationships from prospect to partner. While not a front-line fundraising role, this position requires the same discipline, urgency, organization, and initiative to build the systems and partnerships that drive fundraising success.

Collaboration with Board members, senior leadership, Development colleagues, and other members of the CEO's front office team will be essential to identifying, cultivating, and advancing opportunities. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging with high-level stakeholders, exercising discretion and sound judgment, and representing Women's World Banking with professionalism and credibility in a variety of external settings.

Key Responsibilities

Prospect Development and Pipeline Management

Steward and advance a pipeline of prospective individual donors, family offices, philanthropic advisors, foundations, corporate leaders, and other high-potential supporters, ensuring the CEO's engagement is well-sequenced and well-prepared at every stage
Develop prospect engagement plans and recommend priorities, outreach approaches, and next steps in support of the CEO's fundraising strategy and priorities.
Conduct prospect research and due diligence, developing profiles that assess alignment, capacity, interests, networks, and potential pathways to engagement.
Generate new opportunities through relationship mapping, market intelligence, networking, and creative prospecting.
Maintain accurate pipeline activity, engagement plans, and prospect records in Salesforce and other fundraising systems.

Relationship Development and CEO Engagement

Manage and advance a portfolio of CEO-priority prospects, driving outreach and cultivation efforts through introductions, correspondence, meeting requests, follow-up, and engagement strategies.
Identify and cultivate pathways to introductions through Board members, donors, advisors, partners, and other stakeholders.
Generate opportunities for CEO engagement and help maintain a consistent cadence of qualified prospect and donor meetings.
Work with the CEO to develop the Leaders Circle into a strategic engagement platform for the organization’s most committed donors, prospects, and friends. Optimize the potential for the Leaders Circle to deepen affiliation, increase giving, expand influence, and create a pipeline for future leadership.
Partner with the CEO and Executive Assistant to coordinate meetings and cultivation activities while maintaining ownership of prospect progression, engagement plans, and next steps.
Regularly assess prospect activity and recommend actions that will strengthen relationships and move opportunities forward.

Donor Engagement and Relationship Advancement

Prepare briefing materials, prospect profiles, talking points, and recommendations for CEO meetings and external engagements.
Draft and manage donor-facing correspondence and stewardship communications on behalf of the CEO.
Track relationship activity, commitments, action items, and engagement outcomes, ensuring timely execution and follow-through.
Capture donor insights and communications in Salesforce and share relevant information with the broader fundraising team.
Coordinate with Development colleagues to ensure opportunities are appropriately advanced, cultivated, or transitioned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum 7-9 years of direct experience in fundraising, principal and major gifts, donor engagement, philanthropic partnerships, business development, private wealth, or a closely related external-facing relationship development role, with demonstrated success identifying prospects, building pipelines, and advancing high-value relationships.
Demonstrated ability to operate with a strong sense of urgency, take initiative, and independently drive opportunities forward in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment.
Strong relationship-building instincts and a demonstrated ability to leverage networks, social platforms, and market intelligence to identify prospects, uncover connection pathways, and generate new engagement opportunities.
Experience working with senior executives, organizational leaders, Board members, or other high-level stakeholders.
Strong research and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize information into actionable recommendations and engagement plans.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Experience using Salesforce or similar CRM platforms.
Highly organized, proactive, and able to manage multiple priorities with minimal oversight.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting CEO-, President-, C-suite-, or Board-led fundraising, partnership development, or external engagement efforts.
Experience working within principal and major gifts, executive fundraising, business development, philanthropy, or private wealth functions.
Existing professional networks aligned with Women's World Banking's prospective donor base.
Knowledge of international development, social impact, financial inclusion, or women's economic empowerment.

Measures of Success

Within the First 75 Days

Develop a strong understanding of the CEO's fundraising priorities, relationship network, and expectations for donor and prospect engagement.
Develop an understanding of Women's World Banking's mission, strategic priorities, programs, impact, and value proposition.
Build productive working relationships with the CEO, Executive Assistant, Development leadership, Board members, and other colleagues involved in donor cultivation and stewardship.
Assess existing CEO-linked donor and prospect activity and establish a prioritized prospect pipeline with clear engagement strategies and introduction pathways.
Demonstrate early success in generating and advancing opportunities through prospect research, outreach, relationship development, and CEO engagement support.

jobs.description:
EBC Program Director

The Police Athletic League (PAL) of New York City is an independent youth development nonprofit organization and has been a vibrant and vital institution, serving as an effective, critical bridge between police and communities across all five boroughs of the City since 1914. PAL operates diverse programs for children as young as 2 years old to young adults. Programs include Head Start, after-school programs and summer day camps for elementary, middle and high school youth, and summer Playstreets. PAL also runs evening teen centers and college readiness programs, youth employment, and juvenile justice programs. Staying true to PAL’s roots, a cornerstone of our youth development strategy includes offering competitive and recreational sports for children of all ages. At PAL, we’re devoted to empowering communities and building the best places to work, and that goes for our own teams too.

In its 110th year, PAL continues to reimagine the agency’s leadership structure to ensure the next 110 years are nimble, strategic, responsive, and efficient. We are looking for SONYC School Program Directors to elevate our out-of-school programming embedded within a New York City public school or PAL Center. Locations may serve Elementary through High School youth through SEL, STEM, Literacy, Sports, Arts, Mental Health, and College and Career Access Programming.

This position reports to the Borough Lead.

Requirements

The EBC Program Director is a key on-site supervisor managing all programming as well as relationships with youth, parents, school community, and the community at large. Directors must be creative programmers, skilled supervisors, and skilled talent developers. Familiarity with SACC regulations and DYCD funding requirements is a plus. Directors will partner with the NYPD, DOH, NYCHA, DYCD, NYCPS, and local community organizations. We are looking for individuals who can listen, problem solve and build bridges to partnerships that expand opportunities for NYC’s youth. As such:

Candidates must be dedicated to learning and implementing Best Practices in the field of youth development.
Candidates must be able to support programming that happens during the evenings, and weekends.
Candidates must support the ideas and opportunities of the youth, staff, and community.
Candidates must possess excellent communication and listening skills.
Candidates must work together as a team to support PAL’s programming throughout the entire City.

Major Duties & Responsibilities

Foster social and emotional competencies and mental and physical well-being in a safe, welcoming, inclusive, and nurturing environment.
Manage all aspects of PAL Teen Afterschool Programming including overseeing the implementation of mental health support and inclusion coordination. Use identified resources to support youth with special needs and/or mental health needs, complete mental health referrals, and/or activate inclusion resources.
Recruit, hire, and provide excellent supervision and support to all part-time Group Leaders and Activity Specialists, Outreach Coordinators, and Content Specialists.
Ensure the program is aligned to strategic objectives of PAL, policies and procedures, agency programming calendar, SACC regulations, and the contractual obligations of government and private funding sources including fire safety certification.
Develops a strong Youth Development culture within the Center ensuring voice, growth, and advancement for all youth and staff. Train, conduct observations, and coach across all programs ensuring SEL, mental health, and inclusion policies are being implemented as designed.
Coordinates with the Principal, Director, Regional Director, SYEP Director, and Head Quarters staff to grow creative programming opportunities unique to the Site.
Collects program data, analyzes and drives PAL forward with data driven recommendations.
Ensure strong reciprocal partnerships with NYPD, NYCPS school partner, DYCD, DOH and other Community partners aligned with PAL’s mission.
Plans and coordinates various citywide programs, activities, and special events.
Assists in the development of future funding grants and requests for proposals.
Provides mediation and troubleshooting for on-site issues.
Respond appropriately when time-sensitive mental health services are needed such as suicide prevention, grief, and loss due to death or incarceration of a family member.

Qualifications

What You Bring:

An associate's in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13 OR a NYS Children’s Program Administrator Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR a SACC Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR two years in college with 18 credits in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13.
A minimum of 4 years of demonstrated successful experience in a supervisory position providing services to youth that includes program management and staff supervision with at least three years in a leadership capacity.
Demonstrated skills in program planning, implementation, and evaluation.
Open to learning and growing. All staff will be learning mental health, SEL, and special needs inclusion skills and expected to integrate them into programming.
Knowledge of DYCD Connect preferred. Microsoft office skills are required.
Strong verbal and written communication skills and ability to work collaboratively. Bi-lingual in Spanish, French, or Chinese preferred.
Able to travel to any PAL location in the 5 Boroughs for training.
Work Schedule: Tuesday to Saturday, 1:00-9:00pm with additional days as needed.

Compensation:
The salary for this role is $68,000-70,000 annually.

Benefits:
PAL offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes health insurance, flexible spending account options, an employee assistance program, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, life insurance, retirement savings options, a generous paid time off policy, training and more!

Location: Edward Byrne Center - Queens, NY

Start Date:
August 10th, 2026

Background

Located in the heart of Atlanta, the High Museum of Art is acclaimed for its extensive and diverse programming, and its commitment to accessibility and engagement. With more than 300,000 square feet of light-filled spaces designed by noted architects Richard Meier and Renzo Piano, and a growing collection that exceeds 19,000 items, the High Museum is widely recognized as the Southeast’s leading art museum. As the High approaches its 100th anniversary in October 2026, the Museum continues to gain national and global recognition.

Guided by Director Rand Suffolk and an exceptional team and Board of Directors, the High strives to provide exhibitions and educational programs that challenge and inspire the Museum’s diverse audience of regional and global visitors.

To support the Museum as it continues to strive for excellence, the High seeks a Chief Operating Officer (COO) with strong operational, logistic, and partnership building skills to help guide the impact of the leading cultural institution of the American South. The COO will operationalize the Museum’s commitment to providing access to dynamic and compelling visual art and programming for all.

About the High Museum of Art

The Museum has been intentional about listening to feedback from the Atlanta community while seeking to captivate both the High’s local and global audiences. Since 2018, the Museum leadership has added nearly five thousand objects to the permanent collection, intentionally acquiring works that reflect the High’s current and prospective audiences.

The organizational values of Inclusivity, Collaboration, Connectivity, and Growth inform the High’s engagement with patrons, the thoughtfulness of its exhibitions, and its internal culture. This framework is grounded in a commitment to Atlanta’s diverse community.

Working closely with the Director and other senior leaders, the COO will be charged with developing the systems that support the work of the High Museum, allowing the High to fully engage in its purpose and commitments to Atlanta and beyond.

The Opportunity

The COO will be a leader of integrity, entrusted with overarching operational responsibilities. Strategic and tactical, fluent in data and trends, the COO will play a significant role in the High’s growth and scaling. The COO will be the thought leader in organizational matters, leading efforts for process improvements. The Chief Operating Officer will be a skilled communicator and convener, facilitating collaboration that supports the Museum’s path forward.

Key Responsibilities

Develop a strong, effective partnership with the Director that ensures strategic, anticipatory management of the Museum and its programs.
In consultation with the Director, forge and implement the museum’s long and short-range strategic planning efforts to develop multi-year budgets, evaluate progress of museum activity against established goals and relevant benchmarks, and ensure plans are revised and updated as necessary to respond to market conditions.
Seek out and bring best practices of museum strategic operations to ensure the continual improvement of the High.
In tandem with the Director and CFO, institute rigorous, best-in-class processes in budgeting and financial planning and analysis, cost management, program improvement metrics and/or policy changes. Create strong integration and collection of data and lead a cross-departmental team to understand how data can be used strategically to meet revenue and programmatic goals.
Optimize technology across the organization to enhance and streamline museum-wide workflow and identify technological solutions to automate and/or improve finance and accounting functions.
Guide senior leadership in designing and integrating strategic, multi-year planning and goal setting to achieve desired results and support the High’s objectives.
Provide proactive, creative and effective leadership around increased earned revenue, ensuring the maximum financial contribution of all revenue-generating activities of the High including the store, rental activities, admissions, membership and parking operations while reflecting the institution’s mission and high standards.
Serve as a strategic partner to the Chief Financial Officer to interpret budget strategies and short and long-term goals into operation and program expenditure budgets as well as collaborate on reforecasting and refining multi-year philanthropic revenue projections.
Lead the Director of People Success to support and enhance human capital management efforts around staffing, training and overall organizational culture.
Ensure that all operational aspects of the High are aligned with overall objectives and reflect the institution’s core artistic and educational values; uphold high standards for integrity, accuracy, productivity, professionalism and cooperation in the workplace.
Implement and streamline process optimization and role definition, positioning the museum more appropriately for sustainable growth.

The Police Athletic League (PAL) of New York City is an independent youth development nonprofit organization and has been a vibrant and vital institution, serving as an effective, critical bridge between police and communities across all five boroughs of the City since 1914. PAL operates diverse programs for children as young as 2 years old to young adults. Programs include Head Start, after-school programs and summer day camps for elementary, middle and high school youth, and summer Playstreets. PAL also runs evening teen centers and college readiness programs, youth employment, and juvenile justice programs. Staying true to PAL’s roots, a cornerstone of our youth development strategy includes offering competitive and recreational sports for children of all ages. At PAL, we’re devoted to empowering communities and building the best places to work, and that goes for our own teams too.

In its 110th year, PAL continues to reimagine the agency’s leadership structure to ensure the next 110 years are nimble, strategic, responsive, and efficient. We are looking for SONYC School Program Directors to elevate our out-of-school programming embedded within a New York City public school or PAL Center. Locations may serve Elementary through High School youth through SEL, STEM, Literacy, Sports, Arts, Mental Health, and College and Career Access Programming.

This position reports to the Borough Lead.

The EBC Program Director is a key on-site supervisor managing all programming as well as relationships with youth, parents, school community, and the community at large. Directors must be creative programmers, skilled supervisors, and skilled talent developers. Familiarity with SACC regulations and DYCD funding requirements is a plus. Directors will partner with the NYPD, DOH, NYCHA, DYCD, NYCPS, and local community organizations. We are looking for individuals who can listen, problem solve and build bridges to partnerships that expand opportunities for NYC’s youth. As such:

Candidates must be dedicated to learning and implementing Best Practices in the field of youth development.
Candidates must be able to support programming that happens during the evenings, and weekends.
Candidates must support the ideas and opportunities of the youth, staff, and community.
Candidates must possess excellent communication and listening skills.

Manage all aspects of PAL Teen Afterschool Programming including overseeing the implementation of mental health support and inclusion coordination. Ensure strong reciprocal partnerships with NYPD, NYCPS school partner, DYCD, DOH and other Community partners aligned with PAL’s mission.
Plans and coordinates various citywide programs, activities, and special events.
Assists in the development of future funding grants and requests for proposals.
Provides mediation and troubleshooting for on-site issues.
Respond appropriately when time-sensitive mental health services are needed such as suicide prevention, grief, and loss due to death or incarceration of a family member.

An associate's in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13 OR a NYS Children’s Program Administrator Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR a SACC Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR two years in college with 18 credits in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13.

Executive Director - Dallas Community Land Trust (DCLT)

About Dallas Community Land Trust

The Dallas Community Land Trust (DCLT) is a newly established nonprofit organization dedicated to acquiring, developing and stewarding land for the purpose of creating and preserving permanently affordable housing opportunities in the City of Dallas for low-to-moderate income families while helping to build and preserve equitable, inclusive, and culturally sustainable neighborhoods and communities in Dallas.

The DCLT is a registered charitable organization in accordance with IRC

501(c)(3). The DCLT has an independent Board that is made up of community leaders in housing development and two intermediaries (The Real Estate Council and Communities Foundation of Texas). The Board is in the process of expanding to include additional members who enhance the organization’s prospects for success. Eventually, one-third of the seats will be filled with DCLT homeowners and leaseholders.

To ensure the sustainability of the organization during its startup phase, Communities Foundation of Texas (CFT) has agreed to serve as an incubator for the organization . For a period of up to 5 years, CFT will provide the organization with in-kind back-office support, which includes hiring the Executive Director as a member of its staf f and providing resources to allow the Executive Director to add a team member.

The Opportunity

new_jobs.description:
On-site (multiple locations—refer to Requirements)
W2 Employee
$200K annually

The families who select Alpha surround themselves with trusted advisors in every aspect of their lives. This is the relationship they haven't had yet.

You will become the person they reach out to when doubt arises, when intuition signals concern, or when they want to share a milestone they know you'll appreciate. You will understand each family intimately enough to sense what they require before they articulate it—and you will possess the composure and discernment to address whatever they bring with tact, care, and apparent ease. Over time, your role will extend beyond being part of their child's education. You will become woven into the experience of this formative period in their family's story.

That depth of confidence is not built through systems. It emerges from presence—regular, steady, unhurried. You will be there during morning arrivals and afternoon departures, at evening gatherings that carry weight, and in private exchanges that rarely appear on schedules. You will cultivate a community families want to safeguard, where inclusion feels natural and word-of-mouth recommendations arise organically from the quality of the experience.

Alpha does not follow the conventional school model. Students complete core subjects in two hours daily through AI-driven applications, dedicating the remainder of their time to public speaking, critical reasoning, and hands-on projects. No traditional lectures. No redundant assignments. Outcomes in the top 1% nationally. The families making this choice are investing in a vision they support—but conviction requires ongoing nurture.

You will sustain that dialogue with every family, through every uncertainty, for the duration of their enrollment. If upholding an unconventional approach to discerning skeptics feels exhausting, this position is not the right match. If it feels like the most compelling dialogue you could facilitate, continue reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Take full ownership of the relationship with each campus family—the evolving, deepening connection that ensures parents feel recognized, not merely accommodated
Identify potential concerns before they surface as conversations, resolving them with the sensitivity and interpersonal skill that preserves confidence
Maintain visible presence in family-facing moments: morning arrivals (7–9am), afternoon departures (2–4pm), evening parent gatherings, and select weekend programming
Develop a campus culture with authentic richness—programming, rituals, and interactions that foster a sense of belonging families want to defend
Encourage parent advocacy naturally, designing experiences of such consistent quality that referrals emerge as an inevitable result
Sustain the dialogue around Alpha's AI-driven model with families managing screen time anxieties, skeptical relatives, and periodic uncertainty—not only during enrollment, but continuously throughout their campus tenure
Recognize when a family is not aligned with the community and address this with the same care you apply elsewhere—safeguarding the community is integral to supporting it
Establish the structures and routines this position demands in a setting where operating procedures are still evolving

What You Won’t Be Doing

Overseeing enrollment processes—that responsibility belongs to the Admissions Director; your work commences once families are onboarded and deepens continuously
Operating from a desk—your community presence defines the role
Adhering to standard 9–5 schedules—early mornings, late afternoons, and evening programming are inherent to the position, not occasional
Relying on administrative infrastructure, formalized procedures, or a complete team—you function with significant autonomy and create what is necessary
Approaching family relationships as transactional accounts—this role rewards authentic engagement, not procedural adherence

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Serve as the trusted cornerstone relationship in every family's Alpha experience. Maintain their confidence during challenging moments, foster a community where belonging feels purposeful, and establish the environment in which satisfied families naturally become active advocates.

Basic Requirements

Currently reside within commuting distance of one of these campuses OR willing to relocate within 60 days (preference given to candidates with established local networks): Denver, CO; Greenwich, CT; Boca Raton, FL; Tampa, FL; Boston, MA; Bethesda, MD; Charlotte, NC; Las Vegas, NV; Oklahoma City, OK; Tulsa, OK; Nashville, TN; Austin, TX; Dallas (Carrollton), TX; Fort Worth, TX; Houston (The Woodlands), TX; Park City, UT; Burlington, VT; Kirkland, WA; or Jackson Hole, WY
Legally authorized for U.S. employment without sponsorship
5+ years in a relationship-focused role serving high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families—private school admissions, luxury hospitality, philanthropy, or any context where discretion, warmth, and interpersonal sophistication mattered as much as competence
Proven capacity to maintain relationships through challenging moments with sophisticated families and retain trust throughout
Authentic presence and communication approach that builds confidence rapidly with affluent, demanding families—polished but never rehearsed
Direct familiarity with independent, private, or alternative education—through professional experience or as a parent—that provides credible perspective when families challenge the model
Sincere conviction in AI-powered education and the capacity to express that belief authentically across years of parent engagement, not solely during initial enrollment
Availability for non-traditional hours: early mornings (7–9am), late afternoons (2–4pm), evening events 2–3x monthly, and occasional weekend activities

Nice-to-have Requirements

Exceptional candidates will possess at least one of the following:

Established connections within the local affluent community that provide an immediate, organic entry point on campus
Private or independent school background with demonstrated success in family retention and community cultivation—beyond enrollment metrics alone
Experience managing high-stakes family dynamics where your judgment and discretion were the foundation of sustained trust
A talent for designing experiences—programs, occasions, settings—that foster a sense of belonging to something people want to protect
Prior startup or early-stage involvement where you built infrastructure from scratch and maintained composure through rapid change

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $100 USD/hour, which equates to $200,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly.
